g.text: FIGURE 7: INITIAL/BOUNDARY VALUE PROBLEMS & PDE SEPARATION OF VARIABLES ENGINE
IVP vs BVP, Picard's Existence/Uniqueness, Sturm-Liouville & Canonical PDE Triad (Heat, Wave, Laplace)
GATE 2027 TITANS ENGINE
SPEC: ULTRA-HD 4K BLUEPRINT
1. IVP VS BVP & PICARD UNIQUENESS THEOREM
INITIAL VALUE PROBLEM (IVP)
All conditions specified at a SINGLE point x = x₀:
y(x₀) = y₀, y'(x₀) = y₁', y''(x₀) = y₂', ...
• Always yields a UNIQUE solution if Lipschitz continuity condition is satisfied.
• Models dynamic time-domain evolutionary systems (e.g. initial displacement & velocity at t=0).
BOUNDARY VALUE PROBLEM (BVP)
Conditions specified at MULTIPLE distinct boundary points (e.g. x = a and x = b):
y(a) = α, y(b) = β (Dirichlet conditions)
CRITICAL BVP BEHAVIOR: May have UNIQUE, NO SOLUTION, or INFINITELY MANY SOLUTIONS!
Depends on whether the system determinant vanishes (Sturm-Liouville eigenvalues).
PICARD-LINDELÖF EXISTENCE & UNIQUENESS
For dy/dx = f(x, y), y(x₀) = y₀ in region R around (x₀, y₀):
1. f(x, y) is continuous in R ⟹ Solution EXISTS.
2. ∂f/∂y is continuous and bounded in R (Lipschitz) ⟹ Solution is UNIQUE.
Trap: dy/dx = y^(1/3), y(0) = 0: ∂f/∂y = 1/(3y^(2/3)) unbounded at 0 ⟹ INFINITELY MANY SOLUTIONS!
2. STURM-LIOUVILLE EIGENVALUE SYSTEMS
CANONICAL SELF-ADJOINT FORM
d/dx [ p(x) dy/dx ] + q(x) y + λ r(x) y = 0 on [a, b]
Conditions: p(x) > 0, r(x) > 0 (weight function) on [a, b].
λ represents the Eigenvalue; non-trivial solutions y(x) are Eigenfunctions.
THE 4 GOLDEN PROPERTIES OF REGULAR SL SYSTEMS
1. Real Eigenvalues: All eigenvalues λₙ are strictly REAL (no complex eigenvalues!).
2. Infinite Ordered Spectrum: λ₁ < λ₂ < λ₃ < ... < λₙ → ∞.
3. Orthogonality of Eigenfunctions w.r.t. Weight r(x):
∫ₐᵇ y_m(x) y_n(x) r(x) dx = 0 for m ≠ n
BENCHMARK: y'' + λ y = 0, y(0) = 0, y(L) = 0
Non-trivial solutions occur only for λ > 0 ⟹ y = c₁ cos(√λ x) + c₂ sin(√λ x).
Eigenvalues: λₙ = (nπ / L)² | Eigenfunctions: yₙ(x) = sin(nπ x / L)
3. THE CANONICAL 2ND-ORDER PDE TRIAD
A. 1D WAVE EQUATION (HYPERBOLIC: B² - 4AC > 0)
∂²u / ∂t² = c² ( ∂²u / ∂x² )
• Models vibrating string, acoustic waves, electromagnetic propagation.
• D'Alembert's General Solution: u(x, t) = f(x - ct) + g(x + ct).
• Boundary fixed (0, L): u(x, t) = ∑ [ Aₙ cos(nπct/L) + Bₙ sin(nπct/L) ] sin(nπx/L).
B. 1D HEAT EQUATION (PARABOLIC: B² - 4AC = 0)
∂u / ∂t = α² ( ∂²u / ∂x² )
• Models transient heat conduction, molecular diffusion.
• Separation: u(x, t) = X(x) T(t) ⟹ T'(t)/α²T = X''(x)/X = -p².
• Exponential time decay factor: e^(-α² (nπ/L)² t) enforces dissipative cooling.
C. 2D LAPLACE EQUATION (ELLIPTIC: B² - 4AC < 0)
∂²u / ∂x² + ∂²u / ∂y² = 0 (∇²u = 0)
• Models steady-state heat, electrostatic potential, irrotational fluid flow.
• Solutions are HARMONIC functions; maximum/minimum principle holds.
• Separation: X(x) = (c₁ cos px + c₂ sin px), Y(y) = (c₃ cosh py + c₄ sinh py).
4. BENCHMARK BOUNDARY VALUE PROBLEM DRILL: y'' + 4y = 0 WITH THREE CONFLICTING BOUNDARY REGIMES
REGIME A: UNIQUE SOLUTION
General solution: y(x) = c₁ cos(2x) + c₂ sin(2x)
Boundary Conditions: y(0) = 1, y(π/4) = 3
1. Apply y(0) = 1:
y(0) = c₁ cos(0) + c₂ sin(0) = c₁ = 1 ⟹ c₁ = 1
2. Apply y(π/4) = 3:
y(π/4) = cos(π/2) + c₂ sin(π/2) = 0 + c₂ (1) = c₂
⟹ c₂ = 3
VERDICT: EXACTLY ONE UNIQUE SOLUTION:
y(x) = cos(2x) + 3 sin(2x)
System determinant det [ 1 0 ; 0 1 ] = 1 ≠ 0 ⟹ Unique!
REGIME B: INFINITELY MANY SOLUTIONS
General solution: y(x) = c₁ cos(2x) + c₂ sin(2x)
Boundary Conditions: y(0) = 0, y(π) = 0
1. Apply y(0) = 0:
y(0) = c₁ cos(0) + c₂ sin(0) = c₁ = 0 ⟹ c₁ = 0
2. Apply y(π) = 0:
y(π) = (0) cos(2π) + c₂ sin(2π) = 0 + c₂ (0) = 0
0 · c₂ = 0 (Satisfied for ANY real c₂!)
VERDICT: INFINITELY MANY SOLUTIONS:
y(x) = c₂ sin(2x) (c₂ ∈ ℝ arbitrary)
Boundary points match eigenvalue resonance (Sturm-Liouville mode)!
REGIME C: NO SOLUTION (CONTRADICTION)
General solution: y(x) = c₁ cos(2x) + c₂ sin(2x)
Boundary Conditions: y(0) = 0, y(π) = 5
1. Apply y(0) = 0:
2. Apply y(π) = 5:
y(π) = (0) cos(2π) + c₂ sin(2π) = 0 + c₂ (0) = 0
0 = 5 (MATHEMATICAL CONTRADICTION!)
VERDICT: NO SOLUTION EXISTS!
NO SOLUTION (INCONSISTENT BVP)
Essential GATE Takeaway:
Always check determinant and test for contradiction when solving BVPs!
DIFFERENTIAL EQUATIONS MATHEMATICAL BLUEPRINT // SCALE: 1.0 NATIVE // GATE / ESE / ISRO EXCELLENCE SUITE
PREPFUSION ENGINEERING MATHEMATICS // SYSTEM VERIFIED
